question: What is the primary clinical indication for performing a vulva swab?

options.B: Collecting microbiological specimens to identify infections

explanation: Vulva swabbing is specifically performed to collect microbiological specimens to diagnose infections and inflammatory conditions of the external genitalia. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is early and accurate identification of pathogens through swabbing important?

options.A: It guides targeted antimicrobial therapy and prevents complications
options.B: It eliminates the need for patient documentation
options.C: It replaces the requirement for informed consent
options.D: It guarantees permanent immunity against all STIs

explanation: Accurate pathogen identification allows clinicians to prescribe targeted antimicrobial treatments, helping prevent complications like ascending infections. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following structures is considered part of the external female genitalia (vulva)?
explanation: The labia minora, along with the labia majora, clitoris, and vestibule, form part of the external female genitalia known as the vulva. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h2)

question: Why is the close proximity of the anus to the vulva an important clinical consideration?

options.A: It prevents any localized skin infections
options.B: It increases the risk of cross-contamination during procedures
options.C: It eliminates the need for antiseptic use
options.D: It automatically regulates local vaginal pH

explanation: The close anatomical proximity requires careful technique to prevent introducing bowel flora and causing cross-contamination during a vulva swab. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h2)

question: What should the nurse verify before using packaged sterile items for a vulva swab?

options.C: The color of the outer packaging box
options.D: The weight of the individual swab

explanation: Verifying expiration dates and package integrity ensures that the equipment remains sterile and safe for clinical use. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h3)

question: What happens if a sterile swab tip accidentally touches a non-sterile surface?

options.A: It becomes contaminated and must be discarded for a new one
options.B: It automatically sterilizes itself through ambient air
options.C: It can still be used if wiped with normal saline
options.D: It improves the accuracy of the viral culture

explanation: Any contact with a non-sterile surface compromises sterility, requiring the nurse to discard the swab and use a fresh sterile one. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the standard patient position used to optimize visualization during a vulva swab?
explanation: The dorsal lithotomy position provides optimal access and visualization for examining and swabbing the vulvar region. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h4)

question: Why is clear communication and obtaining consent especially important for this procedure?

options.A: It speeds up the laboratory processing time
options.B: It alleviates patient anxiety and respects autonomy regarding an intimate exam
options.C: It eliminates the need for draping and privacy screens
options.D: It replaces the requirement for sterile gloves

explanation: Vulvar examinations are intimate procedures; clear communication and consent build trust, reduce anxiety, and respect the patient's dignity. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h4)

question: In what direction should the nurse wipe the vulvar area if cleansing is needed prior to swabbing?

options.C: In circular motions starting from the anus
options.D: From side to side across the thighs

explanation: Wiping from anterior to posterior prevents the introduction of fecal flora from the perianal region into the vaginal and vulvar area. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the proper technique for collecting the specimen with the swab?

options.A: Pressing the swab harshly against the pelvic bone
options.B: Gently rotating the swab over the affected lesion or discharge for several seconds
options.C: Swiping rapidly across the patient's inner thighs
options.D: Soaking the swab in water before touching the skin

explanation: Gentle rotation over the target lesion ensures adequate collection of cellular material and exudate without causing undue pain. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h5)

question: When and where should the specimen container be labeled?

options.A: At the nurse's station at the end of the shift
options.B: At the bedside immediately after collection in the patient's presence
options.C: In the laboratory before the patient arrives
options.D: On the patient's chart without marking the tube

explanation: Labeling the specimen at the bedside immediately after collection prevents sample mix-ups and ensures accurate patient identification. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which of the following details must be included on the specimen label?

options.A: Patient's diagnosis code and insurance provider
options.B: Patient's name, ID number, collection date/time, and exact anatomical site
options.C: The nurse's home address and phone number
options.D: The brand name of the examination gloves used

explanation: Essential labeling details include the patient's identifiers, collection time, and specific anatomical site to guide laboratory processing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h6)

question: Where should contaminated swabs and disposable packaging be discarded after the procedure?

options.A: In the general household waste bin
options.C: In the clean linen storage basket

explanation: Contaminated items exposed to bodily fluids must be disposed of in biohazard containers to prevent the spread of infection. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of adhering to strict infection control during a vulva swab?

options.A: To reduce the cost of laboratory testing
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination and healthcare-associated infections
options.C: To shorten the duration of the patient examination
options.D: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene

explanation: Strict infection control practices prevent pathogens from spreading between patients, staff, and the healthcare environment. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h7)

question: What key information must be included in the nursing documentation following a vulva swab?

options.A: The cost of the laboratory reagents
options.B: Date, time, indication, anatomical site swabbed, and specimen dispatch
options.C: The manufacturer of the transport tube
options.D: The patient's favorite meal and hobbies

explanation: Comprehensive documentation must detail when the procedure was done, why it was done, where the swab was taken, and tracking of the specimen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h8)

question: What is an important aspect of post-procedure patient care after a vulvar examination?

options.A: Asking the patient to wait in the examination room indefinitely
options.B: Assisting the patient with comfort, hygiene, and explaining result follow-up
options.C: Leaving the examination table uncleaned for the next shift
options.D: Withholding information about when results will be ready

explanation: Providing hygiene support, comfort, and clear instructions regarding results reassures the patient and ensures continuity of care. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h8)
